records.preferredRestriction: Preferred with PA (PDL p.14): diagnosis-based clinical criteria plus a quantity limit, not an age edit. Oral generics (aripiprazole, risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, lurasidone, ziprasidone, asenapine, clozapine) are marked CC, QL only; approval needs an approvable ICD-10 diagnosis (e.g. schizophrenia F20, bipolar F30/F31, MDD F32/F33, schizoaffective F25.9, dementia, tic, ODD, pervasive developmental disorders) (PA criteria p.70-72). Age limits (AE) apply only to the injectables and to Vraylar. No oral second-generation agent is PA-free.

records.verificationNote: PDL p.14-15 by x-coordinate: aripiprazole tablet, risperidone tablet/ODT/solution, olanzapine, quetiapine IR/ER, lurasidone, ziprasidone capsule, asenapine, clozapine tablet and Vraylar sit in PREFERRED WITH PA; Abilify, Risperdal, Seroquel, Zyprexa, Latuda, Rexulti, Caplyta, Fanapt, Invega ER, Lybalvi, Bysanti and clozapine ODT/Clozaril are NON-PREFERRED. Aripiprazole tablet moved out of paRequired (it is Preferred with PA, not a barrier beyond the pick). Removed "age edit" wording that the oral criteria do not support; the Preferred-with-PA siblings moved to alternatives. Whether the diagnosis edit auto-adjudicates from claims history is not stated in the document, so a human should confirm the real-world friction.]

records.verificationNote: PDL p.14 (PREFERRED WITH PA column) lists the injectable antipsychotics on PA; PA criteria PDF p.78 table shows AE, CC, QL on each preferred injectable. Non-preferred injectables (PDL p.14-15) carry the NPD criteria of PA criteria PDF p.75. Judgment: haloperidol decanoate chosen as the common generic LAI with the lowest barrier among preferred injectables (all LAI preferred agents require PA; no preferred LAI is PA-free). Fluphenazine decanoate is the alternative generic with the same PA. Haloperidol lactate IM (short-acting, PDL p.14) is not a long-acting injectable and is excluded. Injectables are provider-administered; PDL does not state the benefit (pharmacy vs medical).
